events.title: A life that would cross oceans.
events.body: Joseph de Veuster is born in Belgium on January 3, 1840. Known to the world as Father Damien, his life will become the namesake and moral touchstone of a school half a world away.
events.caption: Devotional image of Father Damien · Damien archive. Later artwork, not a period portrait.

events.title: To stand beside others.
events.body: Father Damien volunteers to serve the people sent to Kalaupapa under Hawaiʻi’s isolation policies for Hansen’s disease. His example of shared life and service becomes central to the identity of the school that bears his name.

events.title: Education as an act of care.
events.body: Edmund Rice begins a school for children living in poverty in Waterford. The educational mission that grows from this work eventually reaches Hawaiʻi through the Congregation of Christian Brothers.

events.title: The land already held a story.
events.eyebrow: Returning to the ʻāina · Kapālama, Oʻahu
events.body: Long before classrooms, Kapālama was an inhabited landscape of cultivation and water. Loʻi, springs and ʻauwai sustained communities whose names and relationships remain visible in the surviving land records.
events.caption: Niuhelewai in a later archival photograph. Landscape context; not an image of ancient Kapālama. Photograph date unconfirmed.

events.title: A stream, and a difficult memory.
events.body: Accounts connect Niuhelewai with the conflict in which Kahekili’s forces overcame Kahahana’s rule on Oʻahu. Remembering this place means attending to violence and loss as well as the water that sustained everyday life.

events.title: Names written into the land.
events.eyebrow: The Māhele and Land Commission Awards
events.body: Testimony and surveys preserve the holdings of Kaniniu, Hikiʻau, Waiwaiʻole, Nohunohu and other people in the Kapālama landscape. Their records describe homes, cultivated patches and waterways. An award could contain several separate ʻāpana; it is not the same as a modern tax parcel.
events.caption: Project-colored detail of the hand-drawn cadastral map. Color identifies research layers; it is not original nineteenth-century coloring.
events.status: Primary records interpreted in project research

events.title: A landscape in layers.
events.body: Brown’s Kapālama working sheet brings together older award geometry, roads, deeds and estate annotations. Read it as a layered record of title history: its markings do not all describe a single moment in time.
events.caption: Project-colored Kapālama cadastral detail · Brown 1885 base, with modern research colors and water highlights.
events.status: Primary map with later title layers

events.title: Before the school, a home.
events.body: A surviving photograph shows the Houghtailing plantation house at Houghtailing and Kōhou streets, the present Damien location. Family recollections describe a spring-fed pond, gardens, animals and land used by neighborhood children.
events.caption: Houghtailing plantation house, 1912–1913 · Figure 38 in the HCC report, reproduced from a Honolulu Advertiser photograph. The child is unidentified.
events.note: The child’s identity and the full Houghtailing deed chain remain unverified.

events.title: A school built by many hands.
events.eyebrow: Brother Thomas B. Regan and the founding community
events.body: Under founding principal Brother Thomas B. Regan, the Brothers teach while construction continues. Students, families and volunteers help turn the site into a school. Classes begin in a partially completed building: a community taking shape through shared work.
events.note: The school’s own history confirms classes began in 1962. The project land-history synthesis flags a conflicting opening date in the 2010 report; this entry follows the school chronology.

events.title: Making room to play.
events.body: The project’s school timeline records Brothers, students and families working to transform former agricultural ground into an athletic field. The field becomes another expression of the labor and generosity behind the young school.
events.status: Project timeline; underlying field records to be added

events.title: A home for school spirit.
events.body: Scanlan Gym opens a new gathering place for athletics, assemblies and celebration. The archive’s construction-era yearbook page captures a campus continuing to grow around its students.
events.caption: Gym construction · 1978 yearbook image retained in the Damien school archive.
events.status: Project timeline and archival yearbook image

events.title: The story is still being written.
events.eyebrow: An archive for the next generation
events.body: This living history brings the land, the school and its people into one shared space. The next chapter belongs to the memories, photographs and voices that the Damien community will bring to it.

alumni.title: Lives beyond Houghtailing Street.
alumni.description: A future home for the Monarchs whose work, service and creativity carry Damien’s story into the world.
